Evidence/CLM-047
Evidence record

A change in an external position is not automatically a transaction

What does this evidence establish?

Changes in Yemen's external asset or liability positions should be decomposed into transactions, exchange-rate changes, other price changes and other volume changes before they are interpreted as financial flows. Opening-to-closing IIP stock change alone is not a BOP transaction measure.

What does it measure?

This record sets out a method rule for separating balance-of-payments transactions from other changes in Yemen's external asset and liability positions; it reports no value.

Who or what does it apply to?

Source-specific

When was it measured or observed?

No values yet; this record sets out a method rule

How current is it?

This record sets out a method rule and has no observation date; Yemen's international investment position data are not yet in the public evidence base.

What this evidence does not establish

The difference between opening and closing international investment position stocks is not, on its own, a measure of balance-of-payments transactions.

Limits of the measure

The method is documented, but Yemen's international investment position data and the reconciliation table are not yet in the public evidence base.

How was it produced?

Method drawn from the IMF Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual, sixth edition (BPM6), its compilation guide, and the IMF's published strategy for moving to the seventh edition (BPM7).

When does this record change?

This record is updated when an authoritative source is revised or replaced, a newer comparable observation becomes available, the definition, population or method changes, or the conditions for public use change.

How can I verify it?

How should this record be read?
